heroCommands.comment: Turn a web page into markdown
Add it to your AI tools as an MCP server

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Firecrawl turns websites into clean markdown and structured data that AI agents and language models can read. It can scrape single pages, crawl whole sites, list a site's URLs and, through its cloud service, search the web.
sixtySeconds.problem: Raw web pages are full of menus, scripts and ads, which waste an AI model's context and tokens. Firecrawl fetches pages (including JavaScript-heavy ones) and returns just the useful content.
whoFor: Developers building AI agents that need to read the web
Teams feeding website content into RAG or search pipelines
Claude Code, Cursor or Codex users who want a web-reading tool for their agent
Anyone who wants to self-host a scraping API
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want one tool that works locally, as a hosted API or self-hosted, with SDKs and an MCP server for AI agents. Some features (search, structured JSON, the Agent) need Firecrawl Cloud.
requirements: For Firecrawl Local: Rust and a C compiler (on macOS, xcode-select --install)
Node.js 22 or newer for the MCP server
Optional: Chrome or Chromium for pages that need JavaScript
For Firecrawl Cloud features: a firecrawl.dev account and API key

overview: Firecrawl can be used three ways, and this repository holds the code for two of them. Firecrawl Local is a single program you install on your own computer that scrapes, crawls and maps websites without needing a database, queue or container. The full self-hosted server lives in apps/api and runs with Docker Compose alongside Redis, PostgreSQL and a browser service.

The third option, Firecrawl Cloud, is the hosted service at firecrawl.dev. It does everything Local does at scale and adds web search, structured JSON extraction, screenshots, browser actions (Interact), an autonomous Agent and Alexandria, a library of data providers. The README says Firecrawl Keyless gives 1,000 free cloud credits a month with no API key or signup.

For AI tools, firecrawl-local init detects Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex and adds Firecrawl to each as an MCP server. firecrawl-local serve answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so existing Firecrawl code can run against your own machine.

features.title: Scrape to markdown
features.body: Turn any page into clean markdown, HTML or a list of links that an AI model can use directly.

features.title: Crawl and map sites
features.body: Crawl a whole site into one markdown file per page, or list every URL on a site.

features.title: MCP server for agents
features.body: One command adds Firecrawl to Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex as a tool.

features.title: Runs on your machine
features.body: Firecrawl Local scrapes without a database or container, and parses PDFs and Office files locally.

features.title: Local API server
features.body: serve answers the Firecrawl v2 API on localhost:3002, so the official SDKs work unchanged.

features.title: Cloud when you need more
features.body: Firecrawl Cloud adds search, structured JSON, browser actions and an autonomous Agent.

strengths: Same tool works locally, self-hosted or as a hosted API
Built for AI agents: MCP server, SDKs and LLM-ready output
Handles JavaScript pages using the Chrome already on your machine
Official SDKs for Python and Node.js, plus a CLI
limitations: Search, structured JSON, Interact and the Agent need Firecrawl Cloud
Installing Firecrawl Local needs Rust and a C compiler
The server is AGPL-3.0 licensed, which has obligations if you offer a modified version as a service
Self-hosting the full server means running Redis, PostgreSQL and a browser service

steps.title: Install the build tools
steps.body: You need Rust and a C compiler. On macOS the README says to run this for the compiler.

steps.title: Check it works
steps.body: Scrape a page and print its markdown.

steps.title: Run a scrape with npx
steps.body: If you don't have Rust, the README says Firecrawl Cloud runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup.

steps.title: Scrape a page from Python
steps.body: Use your Firecrawl Cloud key, or pass api_url="http://localhost:3002" to use Firecrawl Local's serve command.
steps.code:
from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY")
doc = app.scrape("https://firecrawl.dev", formats=["markdown"])
print(doc.markdown)

environment.name: FIRECRAWL_API_KEY
environment.description: Your Firecrawl Cloud key, used by the MCP server config and SDKs. Not needed for local routes.

costs.label: License
costs.value: Mainly AGPL-3.0; the SDKs and some UI components are MIT.

costs.label: Firecrawl Local
costs.value: Free to install and run on your own machine.

costs.label: Firecrawl Cloud
costs.value: Paid hosted service. The README mentions 1,000 free credits a month through Firecrawl Keyless.

costs.label: Self-hosting
costs.value: Free software, but you pay for the servers that run it, Redis and PostgreSQL.

troubleshooting.problem: cargo install firecrawl-local fails to build
troubleshooting.solution: Firecrawl Local needs Rust and a C compiler. On macOS, run xcode-select --install first.

troubleshooting.problem: A page comes back with a warning or missing content
troubleshooting.solution: Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium on your machine. Install a browser, or let the page fall back to Firecrawl Cloud.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI tool doesn't show the Firecrawl tools
troubleshooting.solution: Restart the AI tool after running firecrawl-local init, and make sure Node.js 22 or newer is installed for the MCP server.

troubleshooting.problem: Search or structured JSON doesn't work locally
troubleshooting.solution: Those features run on Firecrawl Cloud. Local handles scrape, crawl, map and batch scrape.

bestFor: Developers giving AI agents the ability to read websites
Teams building RAG pipelines from web content
People who want a local or self-hosted alternative to a scraping API
